findings.text: A qualitative note flags this source for review.
The approved daily means span the same days at both stations. The common duration is {{metric:common_minutes}} and the excluded duration is {{metric:outside_common_minutes}}.

Integrating the approved means gives {{metric:left_L}} for Northeast Branch Anacostia River at Riverdale and {{metric:right_L}} for Northwest Branch Anacostia River near Hyattsville. Riverdale minus Hyattsville is {{metric:difference_L}}.

Under the editor’s independent bounds on each daily mean, the lowest Riverdale-minus-Hyattsville volume is {{metric:difference_low_L}}, with Riverdale low and Hyattsville high. Reversing those extremes gives the upper limit of {{metric:difference_high_L}}.

The original USGS series confirm the auditor’s station order, dates and flags. Both stations cover midnight EDT June 1, 2023 up to midnight EDT June 4, including all of June 3. All six values carry qualifier A (approved), discharge parameter 00060 and mean statistic 00003. The daily means on June 1, 2 and 3 were 15.0, 13.8 and 12.8 ft³/s at Riverdale (01649500) and 13.8, 12.2 and 11.5 ft³/s near Hyattsville (01651000). All match the normalized rates at 28.316846592 L per ft³.

Multiplying each original rate by 86,400 seconds and summing gives 3,594,240 ft³ at Riverdale and 3,240,000 ft³ near Hyattsville. The nominal difference is +354,240 ft³. Applying the editor’s ±25% bounds to the station totals in opposite directions gives [−1,354,320, +2,062,800] ft³, which reproduces the litre endpoints after conversion.

Riverdale leads at the published means. The continuous sensitivity interval includes both signs and zero, so either station can lead and equal volumes are possible. The percentage bounds are assumptions supplied by the editor. USGS approval establishes the status of the daily values.

The Northwest Branch Anacostia River near Hyattsville, Maryland, has a nominal discharge volume of {{metric:right_L}} over {{metric:right_minutes}} of valid data.

The interval record’s raw-source digest matches the supplied USGS response. USGS siteCode and siteName identify Riverdale as the left channel and Hyattsville as the right. Both original series identify daily mean discharge in cubic feet per second. Every dated observation carries qualifier A, approved for publication, and its corresponding interval has valid set to true.

Both stations cover June first, second and third in full. Each of these local days lasts twenty-four hours in Eastern Daylight Time. The common window starts at midnight opening June first and ends at midnight opening June fourth, exclusive. The final USGS date labels a complete daily mean. The interval boundaries match at both stations and every requested date is included.

At each site on each date, converting the original cubic feet per second to litres per second using the international foot reproduces the recorded mean. Each assigned error equals one quarter of its mean. Multiplying the converted daily means by the elapsed seconds reproduces the station totals. The editor assigns the independent bounds, while qualifier A records USGS approval status.

Riverdale has the larger nominal mean on every day. On the confirmed common window, the worst-case change in the signed Riverdale-minus-Hyattsville volume equals one quarter of the sum of the nominal volumes in either direction. It exceeds the nominal difference. Either station can lead, and equality is compatible. The marginal method verifies station totals and durations. Matching the original daily intervals establishes simultaneous coverage.
